indicators.note: a formula is a recipe for mixing things, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Einstein is pictured working with energy and his famous equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' points at E=mc², but it is the anagram signal: USING plus E is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein is the standard example of a person of towering intellect.

clue.text: Gross starters, hands down, eaten in such oily manner?

parts.note: the starting letters of the word Gross, its first two
winning hands down means winning without effort

explanation.surface: Gross starters gobbled with no hands in a greasy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes the opening pair of letters of 'Gross', not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Food eaten in a fatty, slippery manner is eaten with grease all over it.

parts.note: 'have you heard the latest?' asks for the news
the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: A bulletin is announced from the newest group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast news report is a bulletin on radio or television.

clue.text: Takes away another man's mail, for example

definitions.text: Takes away another man's mail, for example

parts.words: Takes away another man's mail, for example
parts.note: mail here is chain armour, a kind of arms, so stripping a knight of it removes his weapons

explanation.surface: Someone is stealing another person's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' looks like post, but it is armour, one example of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to strip them of weapons and armour.

parts.note: a design with clean lines is elegant and simple
in cricket a cut is a shot played with a horizontal bat

explanation.surface: A precise, stylish sideways stroke, perhaps in cricket or calligraphy.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut in cricket is a shot played square with the bat held horizontally.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear-cut, sharply outlined distinction is definite.

parts.note: Noah's ark is the most famous boat

explanation.surface: Someone frolics around inside a longboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longboat' must be split as 'long boat', giving L and ARK; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a bit of mischievous fun, a frolic.

clue.text: Fellow with weak spot ailing, with pains all round

indicators.note: the pains word goes all round the ailing word, enclosing it

parts.note: pains are aches
someone ailing is ill

explanation.surface: A sickly man, aching all over, has one vulnerable point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' puts ILL inside ACHES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was invulnerable except at his heel, his single weak spot.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the word sure is to change, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A business is certain to alter its strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' turns SURE into URSE, after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's course is the direction it is steered in.

clue.text: Not the practice of the Cir ole Line?

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: This is not how they run London's Circle Line Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here 'Circle' is O and 'Line' is RY for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory and practice are the classic opposing pair: idea versus doing.

clue.text: Cover up last of the prawn cocktail

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word the
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of prawn are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off the last of a prawn cocktail starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives E from 'the'; 'cocktail' turns PRAWN into NWRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something up completely is to cover it.

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is linked with a Beethoven chamber work.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian prince of the Habsburg family held this title; Beethoven's Piano Trio Op. 97 is nicknamed after one, Archduke Rudolph.

clue.text: One extends the arm of church in outings

indicators.note: the church abbreviation goes in the word for outings

parts.note: outings are trips
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church's arm reaches out in organised outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm of church' looks like a branch of a church, but 'of' is a link and 'arm' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper limb straightens the elbow.

clue.text: Fig-tree in my care, so unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone tends a fig tree, which is a rare thing to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sycomore is a fig species, Ficus sycomorus.

indicators.note: the drop word sits in the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to drop money is to lose it

explanation.surface: A fall in someone's credit rating brings disaster closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a noun but is the verb LOSE, set in CR.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is a comparative meaning less far away.

explanation.surface: Rewards are offered to someone with red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrot and stick: a carrot is a lure or reward; and 'Carrots' is a teasing nickname for a ginger-haired person.

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A big tree, perhaps a birch, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birch' looks like another tree, but it is a verb, to flog with birch twigs.
explanation.definitionFit: To birch someone is to beat or whip them, as a punishment.

explanation.surface: Someone peels the skin off a jar of pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickles' looks like food, but it means awkward situations.
explanation.definitionFit: A graze takes the surface off skin; and a pickle is a tight spot, a jam or predicament.

clue.text: Clear promises of party, nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so the zero letter is removed

parts.note: a political party's promises are set out in its manifesto
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party's pledges come to nothing and are clearly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O, 'nothing', from MANIFESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is plain and obvious to see.

explanation.surface: A space for playing, such as a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play room' looks like a children's playroom; both words mean freedom of movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Play in a rope or joint means slack or freedom; room for manoeuvre is scope, the same allowance.

clue.text: It includes pitchers, making cheap round

parts.note: something base is low, cheap and inferior
a ball is a round object

explanation.surface: Something holds jugs and makes a round of drinks cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitchers' looks like jugs, but they are the players who throw the ball in this American sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball game has pitchers who throw to the batter.

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Friends bond by hitting the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A close understanding between people is a bond of sympathy.

parts.note: ground-rent read as a rent, a tear, in the ground, from which molten rock flows and is left

explanation.surface: A deposit paid by a tenant on the rent for land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' and 'ground-rent' suggest property payments; 'rent' is a split in the earth, and the deposit is rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock from a volcanic fissure cools into solid deposits.

clue.text: A cough mixture for a man up in Argentina

indicators.note: a cough mixture suggests medicine but here signals the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Cough medicine is prescribed for an Argentine man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means mounted on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American cowboy of the pampas rides on horseback.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to untie is to free from bonds

explanation.surface: A news story sets out to liberate the British broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, long nicknamed by its affectionate name for a female relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The British public broadcaster is nicknamed as if it were a fussy female relative.

clue.text: Olive oil said to be good for his exophthalmic condition?

definitions.text: Olive oil said to be good for his exophthalmic condition?

parts.words: Olive oil said to be good for his exophthalmic condition?
parts.note: Olive Oyl is the cartoon sailor's girlfriend, the name said like olive oil; and a bulging-eye condition is a popping eye

explanation.surface: A health claim that olive oil helps someone's bulging eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon sailor's girlfriend is Olive Oyl, and he is famous for his squinting, popping eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon sailor-man's sweetheart is Olive Oyl and his name describes a bulging eye.

clue.text: A small chunk is associated with Egyptian god

parts.note: a nub is a small lump

explanation.surface: A small piece of something is linked with an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal-headed deity of the dead in ancient Egyptian religion.

indicators.note: the letters of the answer are derived from the two words by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A toxin is extracted from a protein.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly-nightshade alkaloid is a well-known toxin.

explanation.surface: Something is at the end of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like final, but it is the verb, to endure. The Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that last well stand up to use; and the Wear is a river of County Durham.

clue.text: For Criterion's first theatre production, take the tube

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Criterion's is used
a theatre production is a staging, here a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The Criterion, a London theatre, opens a new show, and someone catches the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tube' suggests London's Underground, but it is a medical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible medical tube is inserted into the body to drain fluid.

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the USA is the United States

explanation.surface: Conditions at sea as they affect jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-states' looks like sea conditions, but it is two words, the Med and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists name the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish after the snake-haired Gorgon.

explanation.surface: Someone proposes to a woman called Leonora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leonora' looks like a woman, but Beethoven wrote Leonore overtures for his opera Fidelio.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening offer or approach is a proposal; Beethoven's Leonore No. 3 is an orchestral opening piece for his opera.

clue.text: Happened to live on northern slope

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
fell is the northern English word for a hill or mountainside

explanation.surface: Someone goes to live on a hillside in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is an upland hill in the Lake District or Pennines of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that came to pass occurred.
